title: Pre-trained Speech Processing Models Contain Human-Like Biases that Propagate to Speech Emotion Recognition

bias_targets.methodology: Using the Speech Embedding Association Test (SpEAT) to measure the relative cosine similarity between model embeddings of speech from dysarthric (disabled) vs. non-dysarthric (abled) speakers and embeddings of positive vs. negative valence attributes.
Using the Speech Embedding Association Test (SpEAT) to measure associations between model embeddings of European-American vs. African-American speech and positive vs. negative valence attributes.
Using the Speech Embedding Association Test (SpEAT) to measure associations between model embeddings of female vs. male speech and positive vs. negative valence attributes.

Using the Speech Embedding Association Test (SpEAT) to measure associations between model embeddings of U.S. accented vs. non-U.S. (foreign) accented speech and positive vs. negative valence attributes.
Using the Speech Embedding Association Test (SpEAT) to measure associations between model embeddings of speech from younger vs. older speakers and positive vs. negative valence attributes.
Using the Speech Embedding Association Test (SpEAT) to measure associations between model embeddings of human speech vs. synthesized speech and positive vs. negative valence attributes.
